summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by three frontier vendors — OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google — whose flagship and mid-tier models account for the majority of API and enterprise usage, largely because they are broadly available through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI. Open-weight models from Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Alibaba (Qwen) retain massive HuggingFace download volume and strong cost-sensitive adoption. Because much of the live research data references unconfirmed or speculative version numbers, this ranking conservatively uses only model names that can be confirmed as publicly released and currently available.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Consistently the most-called general-purpose model across OpenAI's API and Azure OpenAI Service, giving it the broadest enterprise aggregator reach of any model.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications and multimodal assistants

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Research notes it matches Opus-level performance at Sonnet pricing, driving heavy coding adoption; available via AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and direct API.
models.best_for: Software development and agentic coding workflows

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Described as a context-window leader and distributed natively through Google Vertex AI, giving it strong enterprise reach across Google Cloud customers.
models.best_for: Long-context document analysis and multimodal enterprise tasks

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Low-cost, high-throughput variant with a million-token context widely adopted for high-volume workloads via Vertex AI.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A 671B-parameter MoE reasoning model cited as the cheapest frontier-class model by a wide margin, with massive open-weight HuggingFace adoption.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: Flagship open-weight general-purpose MoE model with very high HuggingFace download volume and strong adoption among cost-conscious developers.
strengths: Strong general performance at low cost

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: Among the most downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace and widely available through AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Google Vertex AI for enterprise self-hosting.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's low-latency tier with strong adoption for high-volume agentic tasks, available via AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: Leading open-weight Qwen MoE model with very high HuggingFace adoption, especially strong in Asian markets and multilingual use.

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's dedicated reasoning model with growing adoption for complex problem-solving, available via OpenAI API and Azure OpenAI.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, math, and advanced coding tasks

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Europe's leading frontier-class model with solid enterprise adoption and availability through AWS Bedrock and Azure, clustering closely with o3 on adoption.
models.best_for: European enterprise deployments with data-sovereignty needs
